name: Today's Report
headline: Rates frozen on a closed Monday: the 30-year sits at 6.89%, up 0.73 points since late February, and Friday's blowout jobs report is the reason it is not coming down.
teaser: Markets are closed for Labor Day, so mortgage rates sit exactly where Friday left them: 6.89% on the 30-year and 6.49% on the 15-year, each one basis point higher on the day. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year up 0.73 percentage points since late February, and Friday's jobs report is a good part of the reason it has not come back down.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Markets are closed for Labor Day, so mortgage rates sit exactly where Friday left them: 6.89% on the 30-year and 6.49% on the 15-year, each one basis point higher on the day. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year up 0.73 percentage points since late February, and Friday's jobs report is a good part of the reason it has not come back down.

The chain runs through the bond market, not through the Fed's podium. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, roughly three times what economists penciled in, while unemployment held at 4.1%. A labor market that strong gives the Federal Reserve room to tighten rather than ease, and fed funds futures moved from about a 49% chance of a September hike the day before the report to roughly 58% right after it. Treasury yields followed. The 10-Year closed Friday at 4.78%, and mortgage rates track that yield far more closely than they track anything anyone at the Fed says out loud.

  • Worth saying plainly: these are market implied odds from futures pricing, not a forecast and not a Fed announcement. They move every day.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Board wide: 2,616 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 232 coming soon and 148 brand new.
  • Five city ledger: 684 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 576 are already on the market and 108 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 260 live, 199 active, 45 coming soon, 16 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,250,000 at $815 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 26 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 183, Milpitas 114, Newark 74, Union City 53.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,071,475 at $694 a square foot. 268 homes are priced under a million, and 148 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: nothing repriced today because nothing traded, but the direction of travel changed on Friday. If you have been waiting for a September rate cut to time a purchase, the futures market just moved the other way, and waiting has a cost. Sellers still hold the advantage on well prepared homes. That said, 148 of the 576 homes on the market have now been waiting two months or more, which is roughly a quarter of the active inventory and exactly where the negotiating room lives.

images.caption: August hiring came in around three times the forecast, which pushed rate expectations up and took September relief on mortgage rates off the table.
images.source: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, August 2026 Employment Situation, released September 4, 2026. June and July are the currently revised figures. The forecast bar is the economist survey consensus, not a BLS series.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Today is the most expensive Labor Day at the pump this country has ever had. GasBuddy projected a national average of $4.03 a gallon when it published its holiday forecast on September 1. The holiday arrived and the actual print came in higher still: AAA has the national average at $4.15 this morning, about 96 cents above where it stood last Labor Day, and the first time this holiday has ever opened above four dollars a gallon. The old record was $3.83 in 2012, which the chart below marks as a line so you can see exactly what is being broken.

Californians will read that national number with a hollow laugh. The state average is $5.86 today, a full $1.71 above the national figure, and the Bay Area typically prices above the state line. Diesel is worse: it set an all time record on Friday at $5.85 and added another nickel over the weekend, which matters for anyone moving, renovating or hauling anything this fall.

The cause is supply, not demand. Conflict involving Iran has choked traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, drone strikes on Russian refineries have cut refining capacity, and the two together pushed refining margins to records and disconnected pump prices from crude. Brent settled Friday at $96.28. GasBuddy does expect some relief once the cheaper winter blend returns after September 15.

A note on the newsletter's numbers, because several did not survive checking today. Market Briefs printed gold at $4,459 and Brent at $96.81. The COMEX front month contract we track closed Friday at $4,476.60, and Brent's ICE front month settled at $96.28. It also showed the 10-Year up 0.02 points, while Treasury's own daily curve has 4.78% against Thursday's 4.77%, a move of 0.01. Silver was left out of the newsletter entirely once again, so we sourced it ourselves.

images.alt: Bar chart of the U.S. average price for a gallon of regular gasoline on Labor Day: 2022 $3.79, 2023 $3.77, 2024 $3.29, 2025 $3.16, and 2026 projected at $4.03, with a dashed line marking the previous record of $3.83 in 2012 and a marker showing the actual AAA national average today of $4.15.
images.caption: The 2026 bar is GasBuddy's September 1 projection. The holiday came in above it, and both clear the 2012 record the headline claims to break.
images.source: Source: bars and the 2012 record line from the GasBuddy Labor Day forecast, September 1, 2026. Actual today from the AAA national average, September 7, 2026. AAA and GasBuddy survey differently and are shown separately.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
There is no tape today. The New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are both shut for the holiday, so the numbers above are Friday's closing bells and they will not move until Tuesday.

Friday itself was a mild pullback on strong economic news, which only sounds contradictory until you remember what a hot jobs report does to rate expectations. All three indexes slipped, with the Dow giving up the most at about half a percent.

One thing already on the calendar: three names join the S&P 500 on September 21, Bloom Energy, Illumina and Everpure. Molson Coors, The Trade Desk and Builders FirstSource make room for them. The entry bar is a market value of at least $22.7 billion.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html:
Crypto is the only market open today, so unlike everything above these are live quotes pulled at 9:14 AM PT this morning with 24 hour changes. Bitcoin is soft near $78,900, Ether is close to flat around $2,475, and XRP is the weakest of the three.

Worth flagging: the newsletter quoted Bitcoin at $79,884 and Ether at $2,511 as of Sunday afternoon. Both have drifted lower since. That gap is exactly why we requote crypto live rather than reprint a level that was already hours stale on a market that never closes.

El Salvador's Bitcoin pile is back in the news. The government tracker shows 7,764 BTC while the IMF counts 6,224, a gap of 1,540 coins that documents attribute to donations and wallet transfers rather than public money. Separately, FinCEN put the running total of crypto investment scam losses at $12.7 billion and wants banks and exchanges sharing information on suspicious transfers. For ordinary users that likely means slower transfers and higher fees, with fewer hacks as the tradeoff.
